references.text: Describes Nimrod's kingdom and the cities he founded, including Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Nineveh, providing direct context to his significance as a mighty ruler.
Direct parallel: 'Cush became the father of Nimrod. He was the first on earth to become a mighty man.' Conveys the same genealogical information.
Uses similar expressions about 'gibborim' (mighty, powerful men) on earth, providing background for the description of Nimrod as 'gibbor ba'arets'.
Tells of the Tower of Babel and the confusion of languages. Babel is one of the cities in Nimrod's kingdom (10:10), and the events provide context for early Babylon.
Mentions 'the land of Nimrod' as a designation for Assyria, one of the few other places in the Bible where Nimrod is named by name.
